draft.title: Stochastic gradient descent on a loss bowl: learning rate and batch size
draft.description: A wireframe bowl of grey level lines and cross-sections shows the loss over two model settings. A red ball marks the current guess. An orange arrow starting at the ball's edge shows the next noisy step and a grey arrow shows the noise-free downhill step. Orange dots trace the current run and blue dots show a saved comparison path. A small dark dot labelled Lowest point marks the bottom of the bowl.
assumptions: Illustration: the bowl is a simple formula and the batch noise is simulated. No real data or real model is used.
Loss = ½(3x² + 0.5z²): an elongated bowl with one lowest point, steeper along x. Bowl height is drawn as 0.8 × loss. The rim is the level line where loss = 3.

Each step moves the ball by exactly learning rate × (−true slope + noise). The orange arrow is that next step and the grey arrow is learning rate × (−true slope). Both start at the ball's edge and are drawn at 3 × their true horizontal length (one common scale).
The noise has a standard deviation of 2/√batch on each axis and is switched off for all 256 examples, so that case is ordinary gradient descent. Because of the noise, the loss falls only on average.
The status reads Diverged as soon as the loss goes above 3, meaning the ball has left the drawn bowl. Without noise this keeps happening for learning rates above 2/3, where the x steps grow.
The noise comes from the fixed seed, so after Reset the same settings give the same path. A run plays 5 steps per second, and you can drag the ball along x only, before the first step.
